title: Collision Course, the new film by Daniel Sánchez Arévalo, premieres on Netflix on 30 October
summary: It was the perfect heist until everything fell apart

###


The film stars Laia Costa, Karra Elejalde, Luis Zahera, Tamar Novas, Álvaro Cervantes and Lluís Homar


Netflix today unveiled the premiere date, first trailer and first-look images from


Collision Course


, the new film directed by


Daniel Sánchez Arévalo


(


DarkBlueAlmostBlack, Seventeen, Cousinhood


), starring


Laia Costa


(


Lullaby, One Love


),


Karra Elejalde


(


Spanish Affair, While at War


),


Luis Zahera


(


The Beasts, Animal


),


Tamar Novas


(


The Sea Inside, Gangs of Galicia


),


Álvaro Cervantes


(


Deaf, Crazy About Her


) and


Lluís Homar


(


Bad Education, Broken Embraces


). The film


will premiere on Netflix on 30 October.


Collision Course


is a thriller in which no one is quite who they appear to be. The film is produced by


Bambú Producciones


(


A Widow's Game, Cocaine Coast, The Alcàsser Murders, The Asunta Case


), with


Ramón Campos


serving as executive producer and co-writer alongside


Daniel Sánchez Arévalo.


The film marks acclaimed Spanish director


Daniel Sánchez Arévalo’s


first thriller. In his own words:


“Do you fancy changing genre?” Ramón asked me. I didn’t hesitate for a second before giving him an emphatic yes. I was really keen to step outside my world and explore stories that didn’t originate in my own head. When Ramón told me the story, I felt that it wasn’t just the perfect vehicle – it was the perfect rollercoaster to take the audience on and try to give them an experience packed with action, suspense, intrigue, bewilderment, twists and pure fun. And I’m especially happy with the cast we’ve brought together: Laia, Karra, Luis, Tamar, Álvaro and Lluís. A true dream team.”


About Bambú Producciones


Bambú Producciones is a production company led by writer and producer Ramón Campos. Since its launch in 2008, Bambú has established itself as a leading European production company in international markets, thanks to titles including


Grand Hotel, Velvet, Cocaine Coast, Cable Girls and The Asunta Case.


Alongside television series, Bambú also produces documentaries, including


The Alcàsser Murders, The Asunta Case and How to Hunt a Monster


, as well as feature films such as


The Chalk Line, A Widow's Game and Rondallas.
